key_insight: The paper introduces an edge-multiscale coarse space inside a hybrid Schwarz preconditioner that remains effective for high-frequency Helmholtz problems.
engineering_relevance: This offers a scalable solver strategy for wave simulations where standard domain decomposition methods struggle as the wavenumber grows.
method: Use overlapping subdomains with impedance-boundary local solves (RAS-imp) in parallel.
Add a coarse correction built from an edge multiscale space derived at the discrete level.
Prove uniform convergence by analyzing approximation of primal, adjoint, and harmonic extension components.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive numerical experiments that test the sharpness of the theory and demonstrate performance on challenging heterogeneous models.
watch_item: The method relies on sufficiently fine meshes for the Helmholtz discretization, with h decreasing faster than k^{-3/2}, which may raise cost for very large wavenumbers.
paper_title: Discrete Edge Multiscale Space based Hybrid Schwarz Preconditioner for High-Frequency Helmholtz Problems
